feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing journalist and activist, has died
entry.summary: Feminist icon and author Gloria Steinem has died. Her foundation posted online this morning that she died yesterday in New York City.

entry.title: Families of the missing in Nepal's flash floods perform symbolic cremations
entry.summary: Eight days after Nepal's flash floods, families who can't find loved ones perform symbolic cremations.

entry.title: Jury is deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy's trial
entry.summary: Jurors in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman charged with murdering her three children, are deadlocked after five days of deliberation.

entry.title: Veteran political journalist on division among Democrats over Democratic Socialism
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with CNN senior political analyst Ron Brownstein about the Democratic Party's division over embracing Democratic Socialism.

entry.title: China's Xi visits Egypt for the first time in a decade
entry.summary: Xi Jinping's visit to Egypt for the first time in a decade, and during the Iran war, comes as U.S. allies broaden their security ties.

entry.title: Ex-National Security Council director on administration's plan for Venezuela oil
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin asks former Obama administration official Benjamin Gedan {guh-DAN} about the viability of the Trump administration's plan for Venezuelan oil.

entry.title: Critics question legality of Venezuela oil deals
entry.summary: Chevron's $7 billion Venezuela bet deepens U.S. ties to the country's oil industry. Critics say the deal poses risks to democracy and could fuel discontent over Washington's embrace of the government.

entry.title: NBA punishes LA Clippers over salary cap scheme
entry.summary: The NBA has punished the Los Angeles Clippers for a scheme it says tried to circumvent the salary cap to pay Kawhi Leonard. The team will lose five years of first-round picks plus millions in fines.

entry.title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-winning jazz artist, remembered
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin asks music critic Nate Chinen <<chih-nen>> about the legacy of the Grammy-winning jazz artist Cassandra Wilson.</chih-nen>

entry.title: U.S.-Israel relations are on the rocks ahead of elections
entry.summary: Relations between the Trump administration and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have turned rocky since Trump called a truce with Iran. Trump seeks progress in Gaza, but Netanyahu is taking a defiant stance ahead of an election.
